elements.evidence: Rendered § 12.4 still binds us: "Neither Party shall solicit the other's personnel directly involved in the Services for 12 months after their involvement ends." A mutual covenant still imposes a solicitation restriction on Customer, so the preferred position (no non-solicit on us at all) is not achieved; the redline deliberately rests at the fallback.
"Neither Party shall solicit the other's personnel …" — the obligation runs both ways, replacing the one-way "Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee".

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Scope is limited to "the other's personnel directly involved in the Services", removing the original "any Vendor employee" all-personnel scope.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: "for 12 months after their involvement ends" — the 24-month post-term tail is deleted and the trigger is tied to the individual's involvement, matching the deterministic duration check (value=12).

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: "General advertisements … are not restricted." The original negating language "regardless of how the employee applies" is removed.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: "… unsolicited approaches … are not restricted" appears in the same carve-out sentence of rendered § 12.4.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The operative verb is limited to "solicit" (the original "hire, or employ" is deleted) and the carve-out expressly states "hiring [is] not restricted", so no no-hire survives.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: all six elements (mutuality, involved-personnel scope, 12 months from end of involvement, general-advertisement carve-out, unsolicited-approach carve-out, no no-hire) appear in rendered § 12.4 itself and not merely in the margin comment.

Preferred is not met because Customer remains subject to a mutual solicitation restraint; that is acceptable under the playbook (a fallback-compliant clause is not further redlined), and the comment correctly flags the preferred position and offers the fallback.

Minimal: a single replacement of the offending sentence, deleting only the walk-away features (no-hire verbs "hire, or employ", 24-month post-term tail, all-employee scope, "regardless of how the employee applies") and adding only checklist language. No unrelated obligation, remedy, or timing mechanic is introduced.

Preserves intent: the narrowed clause is solicitation-only with hiring expressly unrestricted, so it no longer contradicts § 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made "no … no-hire commitment" and that Customer may hire "any person who responds to general recruitment". The separate non-compete in the second § 12.4 (p0046) is untouched and left to its own rule.

Drafting nit only, not a defect requiring repair: "General advertisements, unsolicited approaches, and hiring are not restricted" is a slightly compressed list, and "their" relies on the antecedent "personnel"; both read unambiguously in context. If the counterparty pushes back, consider "Nothing in this Section restricts general advertisements or other general solicitations not targeted at the other Party's personnel, responses to or hiring of persons who approach a Party on their own initiative, or hiring generally."

Severity raised from medium to high because the incumbent clause sat in the rule's walk-away band on three counts simultaneously (express no-hire, 24-month duration, all Vendor personnel) and conflicted with § 12.3.
